title: MeitY consultation paper on AI regulation (announced)
issuing_body: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)

timeline.event: Minister Vaishnaw tells PTI a new AI law is required, reversing MeitY's earlier position
MoS Jitin Prasada tells Parliament safe harbour for AI systems depends on the nature of the service; IT Act is technology-neutral
Vaishnaw announces a regulation-focused AI consultation paper within a month, focused on safety and deepfakes
Vaishnaw says paper will issue in the coming weeks and seek inputs from civil society, citizens and industry
Hindustan Times reports MeitY weighing a sector-specific approach with RBI, SEBI and TRAI setting standards
NDTV Profit reports draft would require AI models to pass tests before launch and carry a 60-day comment window
Paper not yet published on MeitY or PIB

summary: MeitY has promised a consultation paper setting out a regulatory (techno-legal) framework for AI, focused on safety and deepfakes, with sectoral regulators expected to set domain standards. It had not been released as of 19 November 2026.
key_provisions: Announced 8 October 2026 by Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw at the World Development Report 2026 launch; repeated 26 October 2026 at NDTV World Summit
Stated focus: AI safety, deepfakes, a human-first approach, inputs from civil society, citizens and industry
Reported (NDTV Profit, 16 Nov 2026) to propose mandatory pre-deployment testing of AI models and a 60-day consultation period
Reported (HT, 3 Nov 2026) to allow RBI, SEBI and TRAI to set sector-specific standards because risks vary across banking, securities and telecom
Follows the minister's June 2026 statement that a new AI law is needed because the IT Act dates from 2000
confidence_note: Multiple outlets report the ministerial announcements; the paper itself is unpublished. The pre-launch testing and 60-day details come from a single NDTV Profit report based on unnamed sources whose body text could not be retrieved.

title: Draft IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Second Amendment Rules, 2026
issuing_body: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)

summary: Proposed further amendments to the IT Rules 2021 that would make synthetically generated information labels continuously visible for the full duration of content, embed persistent provenance metadata, and create a Significant User-Publisher of News and Current Affairs category subject to takedown orders.
key_provisions: Rule 3(3)(a)(ii) label for synthetically generated information to be continuously and clearly visible throughout the duration of visual content, replacing the prominent label standard of the February 2026 amendment
Platforms to embed permanent metadata tracing content to its originating system
New Significant User-Publishers of News and Current Affairs (SUPNCA) category extending blocking and takedown compliance to individual users above a follower threshold
Comments by email to itrules.consultation@meity.gov.in; MeitY stated submissions would be held in fiduciary capacity and not disclosed
Consultation window extended from 14 April to 29 April and then to 7 May 2026
confidence_note: Draft text and consultation dates confirmed by IFF and SFLC submissions. Whether the final rules were gazetted after May 2026 could not be verified; MeitY and gazette pages were not retrievable.

title: CERT-In Blueprint for Defending Against AI-Assisted Cyber Threats (CIGU-2026-0002)
issuing_body: Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), MeitY

timeline.event: CERT-In warning on frontier-AI (Mythos) cyber risks (reported)
Blueprint CIGU-2026-0002 released

summary: Cross-sector advisory on defending against AI-accelerated attacks. It sets patching timelines, requires AI usage policies and AI asset inventories, introduces an AI Bill of Materials, and reiterates six-hour incident reporting.
key_provisions: Known exploited vulnerabilities on internet-facing systems to be contained or patched within 12 hours where feasible; critical externally exposed within 1 day; high severity within 5 days
Organisations to define AI usage policies, maintain AI asset inventories, monitor shadow AI and classify data processed by AI
AI Bill of Materials (AIBOM) to be maintained alongside SBOM, QBOM and CBOM
Autonomous AI systems to have operational boundaries and emergency shutdown mechanisms
Deepfake preparedness: executive verification procedures and impersonation monitoring
Cyber incidents to be reported to CERT-In within six hours (per 2022 Directions)
confidence_note: Document number, date and contents from MediaNama's reading of the CERT-In document; cert-in.org.in copy not retrieved.

title: CERT-In Artificial Intelligence (AI) Security Auditing Guidelines (CIGU-2026-0004)
issuing_body: Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), MeitY

timeline.event: MeitY says it will tighten AI incident reporting norms, timeframe and content
CERT-In warns AI agents accessed sensitive data at Indian organisations during testing
AI Security Auditing Guidelines released

summary: Risk-tiered guidelines for auditing AI systems used by Indian organisations or processing Indian data, with nine audit domains, defined human-oversight models and a six-hour reporting timeline for AI security incidents.
key_provisions: Four risk tiers: low (advisory outputs, limited autonomy), moderate (annual independent audit by CERT-In-empanelled auditors), high (periodic audits, about every six months), critical (continuous monitoring)
Nine audit domains: governance, data lifecycle, model risk management, ethics and bias, explainability, security and incident reporting, continuous monitoring, human oversight, supply-chain assurance
Three oversight models defined: human-in-the-loop, human-on-the-loop, human-over-the-loop
Reportable AI security incidents (including model poisoning, prompt injection, agentic AI misuse) to be reported to CERT-In within six hours; logs retained 180 days
Applies to AI systems developed, procured, deployed or operated by Indian organisations and to systems processing Indian data or serving Indian users
confidence_note: The PDF is a mirror of the CERT-In document hosted by MediaNama; cert-in.org.in original not retrieved. Contents consistent across MediaNama, Business Standard and Industrial Cyber coverage (4-9 Nov 2026).

summary: A series of Delhi High Court orders in 2026 recognised that personality and publicity rights protect name, image, voice and likeness against AI deepfakes, while refusing blanket injunctions and distinguishing satire from vulgar or commercial misuse. key_provisions: Personality rights protect name, image, voice, likeness and other indicia against AI and deepfake misuse (Devi Prasad Shetty v. Medicine Me, 2026:DHC:8897)
